description.value: A primitive coastal campsite on the BC Marine Trails network near Sidney, reachable by kayak or small boat along the Saanich Peninsula shoreline; arbutus-lined and scenic but not accessible by bicycle without a water crossing.

address.value: 103 E Point Rd, Saturna, BC V0N 0C5, Canada

raw_osm.description: Tent pads in trees. Composting toilets. Picnic tables. Fee charged May - Sept. No fires, including below high tide mark. Sensitive areas have been damaged by trampling, so avoid overflow camping. Large parties should use Princess Bay instead.
raw_osm.description:approach: Choice of 2 easy shell beaches at high water. Rock shelf at low water.
raw_osm.description:other: View. Attractive. Most popular site on island for paddlers. Extensive trails. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.
raw_osm.name: Arbutus Point Campsite / BCMT

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM tags provide detailed campsite information: composting toilets, picnic tables, 6-tent capacity, no-fire policy, and water-access approaches (shell beaches/rock shelf), all within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. The specific OSM website URL (bcmarinetrails.org/map_site/12173) returned a 404 'Page not found' — the organization has moved campsite details to a member map — so OSM tags are the sole evidence source for amenity fields. This site is accessed exclusively by water (paddlecraft), not by land or bicycle, which is worth flagging.
concerns: The specific OSM website URL (https://www.bcmarinetrails.org/map_site/12173) returns a 404 'Page not found'; BC Marine Trails has migrated campsite detail pages to a members-only interactive map, making website confirmation of amenities impossible.

This campsite is accessible exclusively by water (kayak/paddlecraft via shell beaches or rock shelf at low tide) — it has no land or road access, significantly limiting its utility for touring cyclists.
No phone, email, or physical address recorded in OSM.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, publicly accessible campsite within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve with confirmed facilities. Water-access-only nature reduces relevance for land-based cycling tourists but does not warrant exclusion.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM description tag notes that large groups should use Princess Bay instead, and that sensitive areas have been damaged by trampling — overflow camping is discouraged. Extensive trails are mentioned on the island (Gulf Islands National Park Reserve).

wow_evidence: not accessible by bicycle without a water crossing
